name: Fruity Reviews: Product Reviews for WooCommerce
author: fruitysoftware

sections.description:
Fruity Reviews asks your customers for a review after their order has shipped: one invitation, at most one reminder. Customers rate every product of the order on one page. You approve reviews with text, reviews are shown at the product with a notice on how they were collected.

This plugin connects your WooCommerce shop to the Fruity Reviews service. A Fruity Reviews account is required; it starts when you connect. Three tiers: Gratis, free of charge, with 25 invitations a month; Mittel with 500 invitations for 14 € a month; Groß with 2,000 invitations for 29 € a month. Prices plus VAT, no minimum term. Yearly, Mittel costs 140 € and Groß 290 €: two months free, for one year that renews unless cancelled. Every shop can test Mittel once for 14 days, with up to 100 invitations and without payment details. For businesses only.

Reviews show up at the product page by themselves. You can also place them yourself:

  • blocks “Review stars” and “Review list”;
  • shortcodes [fruity_reviews_stars] and [fruity_reviews_list], with product, heading, initial and distribution.

Once you switch on “Take over the display” in the plugin’s settings, the stars of your shop, in product lists and for search engines show these reviews, and WooCommerce’s own review form is closed. Switching off restores WooCommerce’s own reviews; they are never changed.

External services

This plugin connects your WooCommerce shop to Fruity Reviews, a service run by von Heugel Marketing GmbH, Varel, Germany, on servers in Germany. The service sends review requests to your customers, stores the reviews and returns approved reviews for display in your shop. Without the service, the plugin does nothing. The service is for businesses only.

Nothing is sent before you tick the box for the terms of use and the data processing agreement and click “Connect” in the plugin’s settings.

When you connect: your shop URL, shop name, the email address you enter, the name of the logged-in user and, if you booked on fruity-reviews.de, the setup key from that booking. Our server then requests one URL on your site once to verify the connection.

For each order, once it reaches the status you chose (by default completed): order number, time of completion, purchased products, the shop’s language, the customer’s first name and email address, whether the customer opted in at checkout, whether the checkout showed the notice on the right to object, and whether the address unsubscribed in MailPoet. When an order is cancelled or refunded: its order number. No last name, address, phone number, amounts or payment data.

Your product list (name, SKU, URL, image URL) to show products on the review page.

Regularly in the background: a request for orders the service wants to check and products whose reviews changed. When you use the plugin’s pages: your settings and your decisions on reviews. If you import WooCommerce reviews: stars, text, name, date and your reply, never email or IP addresses.

Emails are sent through rapidmail (Positive Group Deutschland GmbH, Germany). Mittel and Groß are billed through Stripe (Stripe Payments Europe, Limited): “Book Mittel”, “Book Groß” (monthly or yearly) and “Manage subscription” take you to pages of Stripe, where you enter your payment details and can cancel. You can also book on fruity-reviews.de before connecting; the setup key from that booking links the subscription to your shop. The plugin never sees your payment details.

Each review has a link “Report”. It opens a page of the service where anyone can report illegal content (EU Digital Services Act); the plugin itself sends nothing for it.

  • Service: https://fruity-reviews.de
  • Terms of use: https://reviews.fruity-software.de/nutzungsbedingungen/wordpress
  • Privacy policy: https://reviews.fruity-software.de/datenschutz/wordpress
  • Data processing agreement: https://reviews.fruity-software.de/avv/wordpress
  • What can be exported, and changing providers: https://reviews.fruity-software.de/daten/wordpress
  • Stripe terms: https://stripe.com/legal/ssa, Stripe privacy policy: https://stripe.com/privacy
sections.installation:
1. Install the plugin: Plugins, Add New, search for “Fruity Reviews”, or upload the zip file.
  2. Activate it. WooCommerce must be active.
  3. Open WooCommerce, Fruity Reviews and click “Connect”. Confirm the link in the email. With this you accept the terms of use and the data processing agreement.
  4. Go through the setup steps: sender, whom to ask, timing, start date. Then switch sending on.

If you booked Mittel or Groß on fruity-reviews.de, enter the setup key from your booking when connecting.
sections.faq:
Who can use Fruity Reviews?

Businesses only. Private persons cannot book.

Does it need WooCommerce?

Yes. The plugin works with WooCommerce orders and products.

Are my existing WooCommerce reviews kept?

Yes, they are never changed. In Mittel and Groß you can import them; they then show with a note on where they come from.

What happens when I uninstall the plugin?

Sending stops. You can still download your reviews for 30 days through the link in the email you then receive, or choose immediate deletion.

Where is the data stored?

On servers of Hetzner in Germany. Details on export, formats and switching providers: https://reviews.fruity-software.de/daten/wordpress
sections.changelog:
0.3.22

  • Reviews without text are now listed at the product too, with stars, name, date and badge, newest first among all others. Before, they only counted in the figures.

0.3.21

  • Stars in product lists (shop, categories, search) once the display is taken over, also when WooCommerce’s own reviews are switched off.
  • Choose whether the stars stand above or below the product title.
  • Reviews: new view “By product” with count, average, reviews with text, waiting and latest per product, products without reviews at the end; every list can be narrowed to one product.

0.3.20

  • “Take over the display” now shows a check first: whether WooCommerce reviews exist (import them first) and whether another plugin also changes WooCommerce’s stars, named.
  • If nothing is in the way, the display is taken over by itself once after connecting, with a notice. You can switch back any time.

0.3.19

  • New name and short description in the plugin directory: “Fruity Reviews: Product Reviews for WooCommerce”.

0.3.18

  • Fix: with “all buyers” and your confirmation, asking past orders now also includes buyers without a consent. 0.3.17 still left them in the shop.

0.3.17

  • “All buyers” now works like the automatic collection of other review services: you confirm once that sending to all buyers is your responsibility, and every buyer gets an invitation, also when you ask past orders.
  • The notice on the right to object from Fruity Reviews is optional with “all buyers” and is shown as fine print. Shops that chose “all buyers” before keep it until they confirm.
  • Every review email states the right to object and that it costs nothing beyond the transmission.

0.3.16

  • Fix: the notice on the right to object under PayPal Payments’ express buttons now also appears with its newer button rendering (SDK v6). It is shown only where a PayPal button actually is.

0.3.15

  • Asking past orders: choose when the invitations go out, now or at a start, all at once or spread evenly over up to 30 days, optionally only in business hours. The preview shows when the first and the last one goes out; planned invitations show the time.
  • With “all buyers”, the notice on the right to object also stands under PayPal Payments’ express buttons on the product page, in the cart and in the mini cart, and above the cart block. Orders paid there right away now get an invitation too.

0.3.14

  • Privacy: while you ask only buyers who agreed, an order without consent no longer leaves your shop, also when you ask past orders. A consent given with an earlier order of the same buyer counts.

0.3.13

  • Connecting: if the confirmation mail did not arrive or went to an address you cannot reach, “Start again” sends a new one, to the same or another address. The link in the earlier mail then no longer works.

0.3.12

  • Reviews from another shop of yours (Groß): you confirm that both shops belong to your company. This needs the data processing agreement of 21 November 2026, which you accept on the overview.

0.3.11

  • Fix: with MailPoet, buyers who did not tick its newsletter box were taken as unsubscribed and got no invitation. Only an unsubscribe MailPoet actually recorded counts now. Orders shipped in the last 30 days are reported once again after the update; the service plans each order at most once.

0.3.10

  • Invitations page: orders not shipped yet are listed first, with when the invitation will follow or why there will be none.

0.3.9

  • Review list: the notice on how reviews are checked is part of the summary, its core always visible under the average, all points under “How we check the reviews”.
  • Stars and bars take the accent colour of the settings.
  • Reviews and bars no longer take the theme’s indent for lists.

0.3.8

  • Setup on the overview: each button stands in the line of its step, the test mail is a step of its own, the figures have a heading.
  • New setting under Notices to you: a mail for every new review, also with 4 or 5 stars and no text (tiers Mittel and Groß).

0.3.7

  • The logo in the review email is shown up to 64 pixels high instead of 40, in its own proportions, so lettering in a squarish logo stays readable.

0.3.6

  • Logo, accent colour and own subject and first sentence of the review email can be set in the settings (tiers Mittel and Groß).
  • The test mail can go to any address you enter.

0.3.5

  • Preview with sample reviews for styling the display before the first real review: switch it on under Settings, In this shop, or open a product from the setup step “Check the display at a product”. Only administrators see it; it never reaches search engines or the product’s ratings.

0.3.4

  • The setup buttons on the overview sit side by side with the usual spacing instead of directly on top of each other.

0.3.3

  • New setting “Form of address”: German emails, the review form and the notices in the checkout address customers with “du” or “Sie”. On sites in “Deutsch (Sie)” it starts with “Sie”.
  • On sites in “Deutsch (Sie)” the plugin is shown in German instead of English.
  • The audience choice sits in the settings table like every other field; “Take over the display” and “Disconnect” have the usual spacing.

0.3.2

  • The line “Reviews collected with Fruity Reviews” under the list is off unless you switch it on in the settings, in every tier.
  • Import and past orders are always visible; the service says if your tier does not include them.

0.3.1

  • The notice on how reviews come about says that reviews with text appear after approval, at the latest after 7 days.

0.3.0

  • Mittel and Groß can also be booked yearly, two months free.

0.2.0

  • First public release.
  • Setup key from a booking on fruity-reviews.de when connecting.
  • Scaffold: plugin header, compatibility with WooCommerce order tables and checkout block, menu entry.
  • Orders: shipped, cancelled and refunded orders are prepared for the service; the order status that means shipped can be chosen.
  • Optional checkbox in the checkout (classic and block) for consent to review requests.
  • WooCommerce’s own review request email stays off while the shop is connected.
  • Tiers Gratis, Mittel and Groß: plan box with the test, the month’s invitations and booking of Mittel or Groß; notices where a function is not part of the tier; in Gratis a line “Reviews collected with Fruity Reviews” under the list.
  • Connecting with the service: confirmation by mail, one key per shop, disconnect.
  • Orders and the product list go to the service; reviews to show and questions about orders are fetched from it every five minutes.
  • A copy of the site under another address sends nothing.
  • Reviews in the shop: blocks, shortcodes, tab at the product page, with the notice on how the reviews come about; “show more” and “report”.
  • After “take over display”: WooCommerce’s stars, lists and structured data show these reviews; WooCommerce’s review form is closed.
  • Plan on the overview: free trial, choose plan and manage the subscription at Stripe.
  • Import of WooCommerce reviews and Reviews.io files, CSV export, setup steps, WordPress’s privacy tools.
  • Terms of use and data processing agreement are accepted before connecting, with PDFs by mail; a new version needs your acceptance.
  • “All buyers” writes only to orders whose checkout showed the notice on the right to object; unsubscribing in MailPoet counts as an objection.
  • How reviews are checked is explained directly at the stars.
  • Merchant pages: overview, reviews (approve, reject with reason, reply, reports), invitations (stop, send again), settings (sender, whom to ask, timing, sending, take over display).

short_description: Get more product reviews in WooCommerce: automatic email after shipping, stars on the product page. Built for German law. Free plan available.
